Row 66 (n=172): "Choose an old man as my avatar and do not change it unless I ask, even after a restart."
SOP: c1 imperative Choose complement n1 (an old man); r1 "as" → n2 (my avatar); k1 "and" c1 c2; c2 imperative auxiliary "do" negation not verb change modifier "even" complement n3 ("it"); r2 "unless" from c2 to c3 ("I ask"); r3 "after" from c2 to n5 ("a restart").

"do" as auxiliary of an imperative clause — hmm, "do not change it": "do" is the auxiliary, "change" the verb. In an imperative clause, "do" as auxiliary is fine (do-support). Is `auxiliary` on an imperative wrong? No; "do not change" — do is an auxiliary.

"even" held as a modifier of c2 while r3 "after" goes to "a restart". "even" grades/emphasizes "after a restart". Per settled case: "A word that grades a linking word ('right behind', 'just above') may be a `modifier` of the clause the relation belongs to." So "even" as modifier of c2 passes. L8.
